column3: The Hebrew introduces the speaker as “he,” without explicitly repeating the LORD’s name.
The Hebrew retains the image of reading “in the ears of the people.”
The Hebrew repeats “God” as the one they saw, rather than using “Him.”
The Hebrew has “the law and the commandment,” with “commandment” singular.
The Hebrew repeats Moses’ name as the subject of the ascent.
The Hebrew joins entering the cloud and ascending the mountain with “and,” rather than “as.”
